## Purpose and scope

This document is the customer-facing design for the UIAO governance
dashboard — the operator and stakeholder view onto control posture, drift,
and compliance status. It promotes the internal dashboard specifications
(the heatmap, systemic-risk panel, and related technical specs maintained
under the governance specs area) into a single design surface that states
**who may see what**, **how long dashboard data is kept**, and **what is
published externally on the Trust Center**. It governs the design; the
technical specs remain the implementation reference.

## Surfaces

The dashboard is delivered as three distinct surfaces with different
audiences and exposure:

| Surface | Audience | Exposure | Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operator dashboard | Internal operators / Canon Steward | Authenticated, in-boundary | Full control posture, live drift findings, evidence links |
| Executive view | Internal leadership | Authenticated, in-boundary | Roll-up posture, systemic-risk panel, trend lines |
| Trust Center | External (customers, assessors, public) | Public, read-only | Curated, non-sensitive posture summary |

## Role-based access control (`AC-3`, `AC-6`)

Dashboard access is role-based and least-privilege. Roles map to Entra ID
groups and are enforced by Conditional Access (compliant device + MFA) on
every authenticated surface:

| Role | Sees | Can do |
|---|---|---|
| Viewer | Roll-up posture and trends for assigned scope | Read only |
| Operator | Full findings, evidence links, drift detail | Acknowledge / annotate findings |
| Canon Steward | All of the above, all scopes | Manage thresholds, publish Trust Center updates |
| Auditor (external) | Read-only assessment view with evidence references | Read only, time-boxed access |

Principles enforced:

- **Least privilege (`AC-6`)** — a role sees only the scope it is assigned;
  raw evidence and remediation detail are not exposed to Viewer or external
  Auditor roles.
- **Enforced, not advisory (`AC-3`)** — access is enforced server-side by
  role and scope on every request, independent of what the UI renders.
- **Separation of publish authority** — only the Canon Steward role may
  publish to the external Trust Center; no operator action reaches the
  public surface without that explicit, audited step.

All access decisions and Trust Center publish actions are logged for audit
review (`AU-2`, `AU-6`).

## Data retention (`AU-11`, `SI-12`)

Dashboard data has a defined lifecycle so that history is available for
trend analysis and assessment without retaining sensitive detail
indefinitely:

| Data class | Retention | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| Live findings (open drift, control failures) | Until resolved + 90 days | Roll into aggregates, then purge detail |
| Resolved-finding detail | 90 days after closure | Purge; aggregate retained |
| Posture aggregates / trend points | 13 months | Retained for year-over-year trend |
| Audit log of dashboard access + publish actions | Per the audit-log retention policy (`AU-11`) | Retained per assessment requirement |
| Trust Center published snapshots | Current + prior published version | Superseded snapshots archived |

Retention is enforced by a scheduled job; purges are themselves logged so
that the act of disposition is auditable (`SI-12`). Retention windows are
reviewed at each authorization review.

## Trust Center page (`CA-2`, `PM-31`)

The Trust Center is the **public, read-only** surface. It exists to give
customers and assessors a curated, current view of governance posture
without exposing operational detail. Its design constraints:

- **Curated, not raw** — it publishes posture summaries, control-family
  coverage, and continuous-monitoring status. It never exposes live finding
  detail, evidence artifacts, hostnames, identifiers, or anything outside
  the published boundary classification.
- **Steward-published** — content reaches the Trust Center only through an
  explicit, audited publish action by the Canon Steward role; there is no
  automatic path from internal findings to the public page.
- **Point-in-time and dated** — every published view carries a generation
  date and the boundary classification, and the prior published snapshot is
  retained so changes over time are attributable.
- **Continuous-monitoring aligned (`CA-2`)** — the posture it shows is
  consistent with the assessment and continuous-monitoring evidence, so the
  public claim and the internal record cannot diverge.

## Summary of controls

| Area | Control(s) | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Role-based access | `AC-3`, `AC-6` | Least-privilege roles enforced server-side on every surface |
| Access logging | `AU-2`, `AU-6` | Access and publish actions logged and reviewed |
| Data retention | `AU-11`, `SI-12` | Defined, enforced, and audited retention/disposition |
| Public Trust Center | `CA-2`, `PM-31` | Curated, steward-published, dated, monitoring-aligned |
